Interactive NHL Shot Map

Saiem Gilani

Source: vignettes/recipe-nhl-shot-map-interactive.Rmd
recipe-nhl-shot-map-interactive.Rmd
On this page

The brief: the recap page for the Stanley Cup clincher already carries the NHL Shot Map image. The web version should let a reader point at any shot and see who took it, when, what kind of shot it was and how it ended, with the goals easy to find and each team’s logo at the end it attacks. The data is the same SportsDataverse NHL release through fastRhockey; sdv_surface() draws the rink, and ggiraph makes the ggplot interactive without losing the rink or the logos.

library(sdvplotR)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(ggiraph)

season <- 2026 # the 2025-26 season: NHL seasons are named by the year they end
cup_final <- 2025030416 # Stanley Cup Final, Game 6

1. Get the data

The same two loaders as the static recipe: load_nhl_pbp() for the season’s play-by-play and load_nhl_schedule() for the final score. This time each shot keeps three more columns for the hover: the shot type (secondary_type), the strength state and the distance.

pbp <- fastRhockey::load_nhl_pbp(season)
schedule <- fastRhockey::load_nhl_schedule(season)

game <- filter(schedule, game_id == cup_final)

shots <- pbp |>
  filter(game_id == cup_final, event_type %in% c("SHOT", "MISSED_SHOT", "GOAL")) |>
  transmute(
    event_type, period, period_time,
    team = event_team_abbr, shooter = event_player_1_name,
    shot_type = coalesce(secondary_type, "unknown"),
    strength_state, shot_distance,
    x_fixed, y_fixed, xg
  ) |>
  mutate(
    result = recode(event_type, SHOT = "Saved", MISSED_SHOT = "Missed", GOAL = "Goal"),
    id = row_number(),
    xg_label = if_else(is.na(xg), "xG not recorded", sprintf("xG %.2f", xg)),
    dot_size = coalesce(xg, min(xg, na.rm = TRUE)) # a shot without xG draws at the smallest size
  )
sprintf("%s %d at %s %d", game$away_team_abbr, game$away_score, game$home_team_abbr, game$home_score)
#> [1] "CAR 3 at VGK 0"
count(shots, team, result)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   team  result     n
#>   <chr> <chr>  <int>
#> 1 CAR   Goal       3
#> 2 CAR   Missed    13
#> 3 CAR   Saved     20
#> 4 VGK   Missed    15
#> 5 VGK   Saved     22
sum(is.na(shots$xg))
#> [1] 1

The page embeds one row per shot, about a hundred rows, so it stays light. One saved shot has no expected-goals value in the release; it stays on the map at the smallest dot size, and its tooltip says so. Blocked shots are left out, as in the static recipe: the feed records where a blocked shot was blocked, not where it was taken.

The rink is the heavy part. sdv_surface() draws it with ‘sportyR’, whose curves (the corners, the circles, the creases) are traced with over 120,000 points, many of them repeats a hundredth of a foot apart. A static PNG doesn’t care, but girafe() writes every point into the page, about 1.6 MB per chart. Dropping each point that rounds to the same tenth of a foot as the one before it keeps about one in six and leaves the drawing unchanged:

thin_rink <- function(rink) {
  rink$layers <- lapply(rink$layers, function(layer) {
    d <- layer$data
    if (is.data.frame(d) && all(c("x", "y") %in% names(d))) {
      key <- paste(round(d$x, 1), round(d$y, 1))
      layer$data <- d[c(TRUE, key[-1] != key[-length(key)]), ]
    }
    layer
  })
  rink
}

rink_points <- function(rink) sum(vapply(rink$layers, function(l) NROW(l$data), 1L))
c(before = rink_points(sdv_surface("nhl")), after = rink_points(thin_rink(sdv_surface("nhl"))))
#> before  after 
#> 122428  20251

2. A tooltip on every shot

geom_point_interactive() is geom_point() with three more aesthetics: tooltip (the HTML shown on hover), data_id (which points light up together) and onclick. The tooltip below names the shooter and his team, the period and time, the shot type and strength, and how the shot ended. The thinned sdv_surface("nhl") puts the shots on a rink with the home team shooting right, and girafe() renders the whole ggplot as an SVG.

shots <- mutate(
  shots,
  tip = sprintf(
    "<b>%s</b> (%s)<br>Period %d, %s<br>%s shot, %s, %.0f ft<br>%s &middot; %s",
    shooter, team, period, period_time,
    tools::toTitleCase(shot_type), strength_state, shot_distance, result, xg_label
  )
)

p_tips <- thin_rink(sdv_surface("nhl")) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(x_fixed, y_fixed, color = team, size = dot_size, tooltip = tip, data_id = id),
    data = shots, alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_color_sdv(league = "nhl", guide = "none") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4.5, guide = "none")

girafe(ggobj = p_tips, width_svg = 7, height_svg = 3.4)

Every dot answers on hover, but a goal still looks like any other shot, and hovering one dot lights up only that dot.

3. Goals that stand out, shooters that light up

Three changes. Misses become open rings, saved shots stay filled dots, and goals become large black-ringed dots drawn last so they sit on top. data_id is now the shooter, so hovering a shot lights up every shot that player took; the opts_hover_inv() option fades everything else. A click keeps a shooter selected (opts_selection()), for comparing where two players shot from.

draw_shots <- function(...) {
  thin_rink(sdv_surface("nhl", ...)) +
    geom_point_interactive(
      aes(x_fixed, y_fixed, color = team, size = dot_size, tooltip = tip, data_id = shooter),
      data = filter(shots, result == "Saved"), alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    geom_point_interactive(
      aes(x_fixed, y_fixed, color = team, size = dot_size, tooltip = tip, data_id = shooter),
      data = filter(shots, result == "Missed"), shape = 1, stroke = 0.9
    ) +
    geom_point_interactive(
      aes(x_fixed, y_fixed, fill = team, tooltip = tip, data_id = shooter),
      data = filter(shots, result == "Goal"), shape = 21, size = 6.5, color = "black", stroke = 1.2
    ) +
    scale_color_sdv(league = "nhl", guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_sdv(league = "nhl", guide = "none") +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 4.5, guide = "none")
}

shot_opts <- list(
  opts_tooltip(css = "background:white;color:black;padding:6px;border-radius:6px;font-size:12px;"),
  opts_hover(css = "stroke:black;stroke-width:1.5px;"),
  opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.15;"),
  opts_selection(type = "single", css = "stroke:black;stroke-width:2px;")
)

girafe(ggobj = draw_shots(), width_svg = 7, height_svg = 3.4, options = shot_opts)

4. Logos, score and headline

Each team gets its logo, score and shots on goal past the boards on the side it attacks, as in the static recipe. geom_sdv_logos_interactive() is geom_sdv_logos() with a hover target over each logo, so the logo gets its own tooltip: the full team name and the shot totals. Its data_id is the team, which doesn’t match any shooter, so hovering a logo highlights only that logo.

club_names <- sdv_teams("nhl") |> select(team_abbr = abbr, team_name = name)
scoreboard <- tibble(
  team = c(game$away_team_abbr, game$home_team_abbr),
  x = c(-122, 122), # outside the boards, on the side each team attacks
  score = c(game$away_score, game$home_score)
) |>
  left_join(
    summarise(shots, sog = sum(result != "Missed"), attempts = n(), xg = sum(xg, na.rm = TRUE), .by = team),
    by = "team"
  ) |>
  left_join(club_names, by = c("team" = "team_abbr")) |>
  mutate(tip = sprintf(
    "<b>%s</b><br>%d goals, %d shots on goal<br>%d unblocked attempts, %.1f xG",
    team_name, score, sog, attempts, xg
  ))
winner <- slice_max(scoreboard, score, n = 1)
loser <- slice_min(scoreboard, score, n = 1)

shot_map <- function() {
  draw_shots(xlims = c(-142, 142)) +
    geom_sdv_logos_interactive(
      aes(x = x, y = 14, team = team, tooltip = tip, data_id = team),
      data = scoreboard, league = "nhl", height = 0.2, hover_size = 14
    ) +
    geom_text(aes(x = x, y = -8, label = score), data = scoreboard, size = 11, fontface = "bold") +
    geom_text(
      aes(x = x, y = -21, label = paste(sog, "shots\non goal")),
      data = scoreboard, size = 2.7, color = "grey40", lineheight = 0.9
    ) +
    labs(
      title = sprintf(
        "The %s won the Stanley Cup, %d-%d in Game 6",
        winner$team_name, winner$score, loser$score
      ),
      subtitle = sprintf(
        "Every unblocked shot. %s shoots left, %s right. Dots: saved; rings: missed; large black-ringed dots: goals; size: expected goals.",
        game$away_team_abbr, game$home_team_abbr
      ),
      caption = "Data: NHL via fastRhockey  |  Chart: sdvplotR"
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, margin = margin(b = 3)),
      plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(color = "grey40", size = 8.5, margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey45", size = 7),
      plot.margin = margin(10, 12, 6, 12),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
    )
}

shot_widget <- girafe(ggobj = shot_map(), width_svg = 8, height_svg = 4.5, options = shot_opts)
shot_widget

The two logos are embedded in the SVG, so the chart needs no network once the page has loaded.

5. Share it

htmlwidgets::saveWidget() writes the widget to one HTML file. selfcontained = TRUE inlines ggiraph’s JavaScript, so the file opens anywhere with no folder beside it (it needs pandoc, which ships with RStudio).

out_dir <- tempfile("sdvplotR-recipe-") # where the file goes; use your own folder
dir.create(out_dir)
html <- file.path(out_dir, "nhl_shot_map.html")
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(shot_widget, html, selfcontained = TRUE)
round(file.size(html) / 1024) # kilobytes
#> [1] 8870

6. A static version

The same plot without girafe() is an ordinary ggplot, so a social post or a PDF gets the matching image: outside girafe() the _interactive layers draw as plain points and logos, and the hover targets stay invisible. ggsave() it as in the NHL Shot Map recipe.

shot_map()
